key_insight: SpikeDS improves 3D MRI prediction of perineural invasion by combining spike-based activation sparsity with window-level spatial sparsity in a dual-sparsity transformer.
clinical_relevance: This could enable more energy-efficient volumetric MRI analysis for cholangiocarcinoma risk stratification, supporting better preoperative decision-making if validated further.
method: Uses a spiking transformer backbone for 3D MRI analysis
Prunes low-salience windows using firing rates to reduce computation
Lets pruned windows still provide key-value context through cross-window attention
evidence_signal: In a 5-fold cross-validation study of 139 cholangiocarcinoma patients, SpikeDS reached an AUC of 0.753 with 14.4 mJ energy use, outperforming the strongest baseline.
watch_item: The results come from a single clinical cohort, so broader validation and real-world hardware testing are needed before deployment.
paper_title: SpikeDS: Dual Sparsity Spikformer for Perineural Invasion Prediction in 3D MRI
